t: Pompeii grew from Oscan villages of the 8th century BCE into a walled town that passed under Greek, Etruscan, Samnite and then Roman influence, and became a Roman colony after Sulla besieged it in 89 BCE.
A severe earthquake struck on 5 February 62, and the town was still being rebuilt when the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 buried it under ash and pumice.
The ruins stayed largely undisturbed until the late 16th century, and excavation since the mid-18th century has made Pompeii a main source for the study of Roman life and urban planning.
dyk: Giuseppe Fiorelli realised in 1863 that voids in the ash were spaces left by decomposed bodies, and devised the technique of injecting plaster into them to recreate the forms of the victims.

f.founded: The first stable settlements on the site date to the 8th century BCE, when the Oscans, a population of central Italy, founded five villages in the area.
f.where: On a coastal lava plateau about 40 m above sea level, 8 km from Mount Vesuvius and beside the mouth of the Sarno river, near Naples in the Campania region of Italy.
f.known: Burial under volcanic ash and pumice in 79 CE; Oscan, Greek, Etruscan, Samnite and Roman rule; siege by Sulla in 89 BCE; the earthquake of 62 CE; wine and oil trade; graffiti in colloquial Latin; plaster casts of the dead
f.today: The ruins lie in the municipality of Pompei and form a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
